You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller's SPA positions and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge deal team
**Status:** Privileged working draft for internal use. Based solely on the Seller's cover note and Disclosure Letter; I have not seen the underlying DD documents (DD-002 to DD-012) or the full SPA draft, so several points below are flagged for verification against the data room.

---

## 0. Preliminary point: the "FINAL / market-standard" framing

Before the substance, note how the Seller's package is framed:

- The preamble asserts these positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams," are "marked FINAL" and "not intended to be re-opened." **Please confirm with our principals whether any of this was actually agreed.** Nothing in our baseline (100% / AUD 24m / debt-free, cash-free / NSW law) records agreement on caps, baskets, time limits or knowledge qualifiers. Unless our side confirms otherwise, treat every "FINAL" position as the Seller's opening position.
- The "market context" paragraph is advocacy, not advice. A 20% cap, 1% basket and 18 months are within the range seen on *seller-friendly* mid-market deals, usually alongside W&I insurance. They are not a neutral benchmark, and the package as a whole (caps + general disclosure + constructive-knowledge bar + all-claims sweep) is well outside what a buyer should accept.
- Paragraph 11 of the Disclosure Letter (the Buyer "must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record") is actually helpful to us: it concedes the disclosures are not conclusions. We should hold the Seller to that when it later says a matter "is addressed" or "not expected to be material."

---

## 1. Liability regime (cl 12.1 – 12.3 / 13) – the structural problem

The individual numbers are negotiable; the **architecture** is the real issue. Four features combine to make the warranty package close to illusory:

| Seller position | Why it is a problem for us |
|---|---|
| General cap 20% (AUD 4.8m) | Low for a deal with no W&I cover and several *known* exposures (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006). Also, if the Seller is a venture vehicle that will distribute proceeds, the real cap is the Seller's post-completion solvency, not 20%. |
| De minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k operating as a **deductible** ("only the excess … is recoverable") | A AUD 25k de minimis on a AUD 24m target is high and, read with the three AUD 110k "related" Sandbar items, shows how claims can be fragmented. The deductible structure means the first AUD 250k of loss is simply gifted to the Seller. |
| 18 months for general claims, and "any limitation applies to **all Claims** unless expressly stated otherwise" | The catch-all sweeps fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, fraud and price-adjustment claims into the general 18-month / 20% regime by default. This is the single most damaging drafting device in the package. |
| Title/capacity warranties subject to the same caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity" | Not a simplification; it caps our recovery for not actually owning the company at 20% of what we paid for it. |

**Recommended position:**

- **Tiered regime, expressly stated:** (a) Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, share capital, no encumbrances, ownership of core IP) – 100% of price, no basket/de minimis, limitation 6 years or statutory; (b) Tax warranties and tax indemnity – 100% of price, 7 years / expiry of ATO amendment periods plus 3 months, no basket; (c) Specific indemnities (section 3 below) – outside caps, basket and general time limits, or separately capped at a negotiated figure; (d) General warranties – open at 50% (land at 30–35% if the Seller offers robust specific indemnities and escrow), 24 months (so at least one full audit cycle post-completion falls inside the period).
- **Basket to tip, not deduct**, set at ~0.5% (AUD 120k); de minimis AUD 10k, with express aggregation of claims arising from the same or related facts.
- **Reverse the default:** "The limitations in this clause 12 apply only to General Warranty Claims and do not apply to Fundamental Warranty Claims, Tax Claims, Specific Indemnity Claims, claims under the Completion Accounts/leakage provisions, or claims arising from fraud, dishonesty or wilful concealment."
- **Credit support:** escrow/retention of 10–15% of price for 24 months (or a parent/fund guarantee), given the Seller is a holding vehicle. This matters more than the headline cap percentage.

## 2. Exclusive remedy, non-reliance and buyer knowledge (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 / 8.3 / Sch 7)

- **"All Claims of any nature" (9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5):** same point as above – the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language must carve out fraud, specific indemnities, price adjustment/leakage, pre-completion covenants and restraints. Note also that a non-reliance clause cannot contractually exclude liability under s 18 ACL (misleading or deceptive conduct); drafting that purports to do so should be resisted both because it overreaches and because it signals an intent to rely on it later.
- **Buyer knowledge (8.3):** reject in full. As drafted it extends to (i) advisers' knowledge, (ii) *constructive* knowledge ("discoverable from the data room"), and (iii) public records. Combined with general disclosure of the whole data room, it means every warranty is qualified by everything we were ever shown or could have found. Our position: knowledge is no defence; the only qualification to warranties is **fair disclosure** in the Disclosure Letter. Fallback (strong resistance): actual knowledge of two or three named Wattlebridge individuals, excluding advisers and excluding constructive knowledge.
- **General disclosure (Sch 7 / DL 1.1–1.2):** reject general disclosure of the data room and of "publicly searchable corporate records." Insist on a **fair disclosure standard** – matters disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely effect – against specific warranties. If any general disclosure is conceded, limit it to the Disclosure Letter, the Accounts, and an ASIC search of the Company on a stated date. Also note the data room cut-off is **22 September 2026 – six weeks ago.** We need (i) a bring-down/second disclosure letter at completion with (ii) a Buyer termination right (and no release from liability) if new disclosures are material; the Seller should not be able to disclose its way out of a warranty between signing and completion.
- **DL 1.4 (non-admission):** acceptable in itself, but add that disclosure of a matter does not reduce liability under any specific indemnity covering that matter. Otherwise the Seller will argue the Ironquay, DD-006 and bonus items are "disclosed" and therefore not recoverable.

## 3. Specific known exposures – "addressed" vs actually addressed

The cover note says each of these is handled. The Disclosure Letter, read carefully, says the opposite in every case.

**(a) Bluefen (cl 3 / 6.3) – 30% of revenue, ~AUD 3.6m.**
Cover note: "addressed … reasonable endeavours … satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent." Disclosure Letter: no consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Issues: "reasonable endeavours" is the weakest standard; the condition is "satisfied" on *any* written consent, even one conditional on price concessions or a change of terms; and we are 30% of revenue away from the business we priced.
*Push for:* hard condition precedent – unconditional written consent from Bluefen (or consent on conditions acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably), Buyer sole right to waive; "all reasonable endeavours" with Buyer participation in communications; long-stop date; warranty that Bluefen has not indicated an intention to terminate, reduce volumes or renegotiate; and consider a deferred/contingent component of price if Bluefen's position cannot be confirmed before signing.

**(b) Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7) – ~AUD 3.2m.**
Cover note: release "to be provided following Completion." Disclosure Letter: not repaid, no discharge in the data room, change-of-control clause 8.1. Under a debt-free/cash-free deal this is simply wrong: the facility must be repaid **at completion out of the purchase price via the funds flow**, against a payoff letter, executed deed of release and PPSR discharge (or irrevocable undertaking to discharge) delivered at completion. Cl 8.1 may make completion itself an event of default – we need Riverlark's waiver/consent before completion, not after. **Verify whether Riverlark holds security over the *shares* (i.e., a charge given by Harbourglass)** – if so this is also a title issue (section 4). Also check for any guarantees given by the Company to Riverlark that must be released.

**(c) DD-005 completion bonuses – AUD 420,000 (+ on-costs).**
Cover note: "a matter for the Seller … not separately itemised." If they are not in the funds flow, the Company pays them after completion and *we* bear them. They are transaction-triggered liabilities and must be treated as Transaction Expenses/debt-like items in the price mechanism (or paid by the Seller at completion through the funds flow), **grossed up** for superannuation guarantee (12%), NSW payroll tax (5.45%) and PAYG withholding, with a Seller indemnity for any shortfall. Confirm whether any element is a post-completion retention we are happy to fund as a retention tool – if so, allocate it expressly and exclude it from the deduction.

**(d) Ironquay / SOW3 IP (cl 11.1) – AUD 180,000 open.**
This is potentially a **title-to-core-IP** problem, not a AUD 180k payables problem. Under DD-004 cl 7.3, the SOW3 Project Materials do not transfer until all SOW3 fees are paid; the data room shows AUD 180k unpaid and no assignment. An indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" covers the wrong risk.
*Push for:* completion deliverable (or CP) of (i) evidence of cleared payment, (ii) confirmatory deed of assignment from Ironquay including moral-rights consents and waiver of any lien; the AUD 180k treated as debt-like/paid by the Seller; a specific indemnity for all loss arising from any defect in the Company's title to or right to use the Project Materials (third-party claims, re-procurement, injunction) outside the general cap; and the IP ownership warranty treated as fundamental and not qualified by disclosure of this matter.

**(e) DD-006 export/privacy incident – ~1,240 records.**
Cover note: "preliminary … not expected to be material." Disclosure Letter: unknown whether accessed, unknown scope, unknown whether notification required, investigation still preliminary – and the incident pre-dates 22 September. The Company (revenue ~AUD 12m) is an APP entity. The Notifiable Data Breaches regime requires a suspected eligible breach to be assessed within **30 days**; that window has almost certainly closed. We need to know, before signing, whether the assessment was completed, what it concluded and whether OAIC and affected individuals were notified. Also check customer-contract notification obligations (Bluefen in particular) and the 2024 Privacy Act amendments (increased penalties; statutory tort for serious invasions of privacy from June 2025).
*Push for:* pre-signing production of the completed assessment; pre-completion covenant to complete and share the investigation and make any required notifications; a specific indemnity (outside caps, basket and 18 months) for all loss arising from the incident – regulator action, notification and remediation costs, customer claims, credits/terminations; and data-protection warranties not qualified by disclosure of DD-006.

**(f) Sandbar renewals – 3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000.**
The Disclosure Letter asks us to read DD-008 and DD-011 "together for timing/scope" and conspicuously does not say whether they are committed, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course. Three identical "related" items just over the de minimis threshold warrant scrutiny: confirm when they were entered into (pre/post accounts date), whether they are in the pipeline of ordinary operating cost already reflected in the price, whether there are termination fees, and whether they duplicate existing services. Ensure the conduct-of-business covenant captures them (Buyer consent for commitments > AUD 50k), and confirm the de minimis aggregates related items.

**(g) Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** Lower risk, but verify the clauses ourselves rather than accept the Seller's characterisation. Lease: ensure the notification is given pre-completion by the Seller/Company and confirm there is no deemed-assignment or change-of-control provision. Mossvale: an assignment restriction alone is usually not triggered by a share sale, but check for change-of-control, "control" definitions and key-person provisions. Obtain a warranty listing all contracts with change-of-control or termination rights triggered by the transaction, with Bluefen and Mossvale specifically scheduled.

## 4. Title and completion mechanics

- **Title.** A share register is prima facie evidence only, and the Disclosure Letter expressly disclaims any Buyer verification. We should complete our own verification: ASIC company extract and historical extract, constitution (pre-emptive rights, transfer restrictions, director approval of transfers), share certificates, PPSR searches against both the Company and Harbourglass (any Riverlark or other security over shares), and confirmation there are no options, convertible notes, ESOP interests or shareholder agreements. Title warranties must be absolute and uncapped (section 1).
- **Price mechanism.** "Debt-free/cash-free" is asserted but the mechanics (completion accounts vs locked box, Net Debt and Working Capital definitions) are not described. The Net Debt / Transaction Expenses definitions must expressly capture: Riverlark principal, interest and break costs; DD-005 bonuses grossed up for on-costs; the Ironquay AUD 180k; any accrued but unpaid Sandbar amounts; unpaid tax for pre-completion periods; and any incident-related costs incurred pre-completion.
- **Completion deliverables.** Add: Riverlark payoff letter, deed of release and PPSR discharge; Ironquay assignment deed and payment evidence; Bluefen consent; signed share transfer and share certificate; director/secretary resignations and board minutes; DD-006 investigation report; bring-down disclosure letter.

## 5. Tax

"Settled under the general regime" is not acceptable. Standard buyer position in NSW/Australian practice: a separate tax indemnity for all pre-completion tax (including the Riverlark and bonus items and any FBT/payroll tax exposures), 7-year limitation, cap at 100% of price, no basket/de minimis, and no knowledge or disclosure qualification. Confirm the Company's GST grouping, loss position and any Division 7A or R&D tax incentive claims (common in SaaS targets) through our tax DD.

---

## Summary of recommendations (in priority order)

1. **Do not accept the "FINAL" framing.** Confirm internally that nothing beyond price/structure/law was agreed at principal level; respond that the liability package is open.
2. **Fix the architecture before the numbers:** tiered caps and time limits (fundamental/title/IP and tax at 100% and 6–7 years; specific indemnities outside the regime; general warranties 24 months); delete the "applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise" default and reverse it; carve fraud, indemnities and price adjustment out of exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions.
3. **General cap:** open at 50%, tipping basket at ~0.5%, de minimis AUD 10k with aggregation; back it with a 10–15% escrow or parent guarantee for 24 months.
4. **Delete cl 8.3 (buyer knowledge)** and general disclosure of the data room/public records; require fair disclosure against specific warranties; require a bring-down disclosure letter with a Buyer termination right and no liability release.
5. **Bluefen:** unconditional consent as a hard CP in the Buyer's discretion; stronger endeavours; consider price protection if not resolved pre-signing.
6. **Riverlark:** repay at completion through the funds flow with release and PPSR discharge delivered at completion; obtain change-of-control waiver pre-completion; check for security over the shares.
7. **Bonuses, Ironquay AUD 180k and other transaction-triggered amounts** to be itemised in the funds flow as Seller costs/debt-like items, grossed up for on-costs, with Seller indemnity.
8. **Ironquay:** confirmatory IP assignment as a completion deliverable; indemnity for title defects, not just the AUD 180k; IP ownership treated as fundamental.
9. **DD-006:** demand the completed NDB assessment now; specific uncapped indemnity; data-protection warranties unqualified by this disclosure.
10. **Sandbar / lease / Mossvale:** diligence the underlying documents ourselves; schedule change-of-control contracts in a warranty; tighten the conduct-of-business covenant.
11. **Tax:** separate indemnity and warranty regime at 100% / 7 years.
12. **Title:** complete our own ASIC, constitution and PPSR verification; title warranty absolute and uncapped.

If helpful, the next step is for me to turn items 1–4 into a riders-based mark-up of clauses 8, 9, 12, 13 and 20 and a revised Schedule 7 disclosure standard, and items 5–9 into a CP/completion-deliverables schedule and a Net Debt/Transaction Expenses definition for the price mechanism.
=== END ADVICE ===
